prompt: What does a rule like *Do not use the category other unless you have to* leave unsaid?

choices.text: Which category is `other`
choices.why: It names `other`; that is the one thing it says.

choices.text: When you have to, and what to use instead
choices.why: Right: it marks what to avoid and not the target.

choices.text: That `other` is one of the five labels the reply must choose from
choices.why: The label list says that a few lines above.

choices.text: How long the summary should be
choices.why: Another rule, another decision.

prompt: According to `lint.py`, how many of the thirteen rules in `v8-rules.txt` say only what not to do?
hint: Read the finding that lists them.

prompt: Why did `lint.py` not report lines 12 and 13 as a contradiction?

choices.text: Because the two lines are not next to each other in the file
choices.why: Distance has nothing to do with it; lines 4 and 16 were caught in lesson 2.

choices.text: *Never* and *always* are not on its list of opposites
choices.why: Right: it matches words, and those are only on its shouting list.

choices.text: Because the lines do not actually contradict each other
choices.why: For `t22` they do: a question about money.

choices.text: Because capitals are ignored by the contradiction check
choices.why: The contradiction check ignores case; it simply has no such pair.

prompt: `t22` asks whether a gift card and a credit card can be used on one order. What do lines 12 and 13 of the rules say its urgency is?

choices.text: Low, because line 12 comes first in the file and is read first
choices.why: Order in the file settles nothing; the rules are both absolute.

choices.text: High, because line 13 is about money
choices.why: Line 12 forbids exactly that for a question.

choices.text: Both, with nothing to break the tie
choices.why: Right: two absolute rules that cannot both hold.

choices.text: Normal, the value between the two rules
choices.why: No rule says normal; that would be a compromise nobody wrote.

prompt: How does `v8-guide.txt` describe each category?

choices.text: By who answers it
choices.why: Right: the accounts desk, the warehouse, whoever runs the website.

choices.text: By three example messages for each one
choices.why: The guide has no examples; lesson 1 used examples.

choices.text: By the keywords that should send a message there
choices.why: It describes the job, not words to match.

choices.text: By how urgent messages in it usually are
choices.why: Urgency gets its own paragraph, about harm.

prompt: How does the guide's principle settle the urgency of `t22`, where the rule list contradicts itself?

choices.text: It has a rule that questions are low
choices.why: It has no rule about questions at all.

choices.text: Nobody is out of pocket and it will keep a day, so low
choices.why: Right: one principle covers both rules' cases and their collision.

choices.text: It sends every question about payment to billing as high
choices.why: Harm, not topic, decides urgency in the guide.

choices.text: It leaves urgency to the model's judgement, with no guidance
choices.why: It gives a principle and two instances of it.

prompt: `stats.py` reports a mean of 231.3 tokens in for the rules and 285.3 for the guide. How many tokens longer, per call, is the guide's prompt?
Lesson 2 cut 97 tokens from a prompt and lost nothing; the guide is 54 tokens longer than the rules. Why is that consistent?

choices.text: Because shorter prompts are always better, so the guide is a mistake
choices.why: The test of a line is whether it changes an answer, not its length.

choices.text: The lines removed then decided nothing
choices.why: Right, and whether they change answers is then measured.

choices.text: Because tokens of explanation are cheaper than tokens of rules
choices.why: A token is a token.

choices.text: Because the guide replaced the label lists with prose
choices.why: The guide keeps the label lists as they are.

prompt: Over seventy cases the rules passed 27 and the guide 31, with `p = 0.289` on the eight that changed. What is the right report?

choices.text: The guide is better by four messages
choices.why: Four messages in eight changes is what a coin does about three times in ten.

choices.text: The guide does not work
choices.why: Not detecting a difference is not showing there is none.

choices.text: No difference detected on seventy cases
choices.why: Right, with what the totals hide reported beside it.

choices.text: The rules are better, because they got `t22` right
choices.why: One message settles nothing either way.

prompt: The rules and the guide scored within four of each other. What did the urgency failures show underneath?

choices.text: Both made the same mistakes on the same messages
choices.why: Eleven categories differed, and the urgency errors went opposite ways.

choices.text: Rules pushed it down, the guide up
choices.why: Right: 15 too low and 10 too high against 8 and 15.

choices.text: The guide fixed every urgency the rules got wrong
choices.why: It got 23 urgencies wrong to the rules' 25.

choices.text: Neither prompt changed any urgency
choices.why: Both prompts got urgencies wrong, in different directions.

prompt: The guide was argued from `t22`, and on `llama3.2:3b` the rules got `t22` right and the guide did not. What do you do with that?

choices.text: Report it as a prediction that failed on this model
choices.why: Right: a result to report, not to explain away.

choices.text: Remove `t22` from the test set, since it is one message
choices.why: Removing the case that disagrees with you is how a test set stops being a test.

choices.text: Conclude that rules are better than explanations
choices.why: One message settles nothing, and the totals point the other way.

choices.text: Run it again until the guide gets it right
choices.why: At temperature 0 it repeats; rerunning until you like the answer is not measuring.

prompt: Of the 70 messages, only the ___ whose results changed between the two runs carry evidence about which prompt is better.
Read as written, which category does the rule list give `h01`, a refund paid to the wrong card after a return?

choices.text: billing
choices.why: That is the person's label, and what the guide's reason points to.

choices.text: returns
choices.why: Right: line 18, a refund for a returned book is returns.

choices.text: account
choices.why: Nothing about signing in or settings.

choices.text: other
choices.why: Line 10 tells the reader to avoid `other`.

prompt: What does a reason written beside a rule give the person who maintains the prompt?

choices.text: A way to tell when it stops applying
choices.why: Right: without the reason nobody dares delete it.

choices.text: A guarantee that the model follows it
choices.why: `h01` shows a reason the model did not use.

choices.text: A shorter prompt
choices.why: A reason makes a line longer.

choices.text: Protection from the linter
choices.why: The linter reads words, not reasons.

prompt: Where does the lesson say reasons belong in a prompt?

choices.text: Where the reader has to use judgement
choices.why: Right: which desk, how urgent, what the summary is for.

choices.text: On every line, including the label lists
choices.why: The label lists and the JSON shape are a contract: stated, not argued.

choices.text: Only in a comment the model never sees
choices.why: The model is one of the readers.

choices.text: In a separate document beside the prompt
choices.why: Beside the rule, in the prompt, is the point.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson cite from Anthropic's prompt engineering documentation? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Give the model the context and motivation behind an instruction
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Say what to do rather than only what not to do
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Explanations measurably beat rules by a stated percentage
choices.why: The documentation presents it as guidance, not a measured gain.

choices.text: Put the most important rule in capitals
choices.why: Capitals are one of the problems the lesson names.

prompt: Both prompts sorted `h01` as `returns`, though the guide's line 10 points to billing. What does that say about writing reasons into a prompt?

choices.text: Reasons are useless and should be removed
choices.why: They still serve the person who maintains the prompt, and another model may use them.

choices.text: A reader able to use it is not a reader using it
choices.why: Right: whether the model applies it is measured, not assumed.

choices.text: The guide needs line 10 in capitals
choices.why: Capitals rank a rule; they do not make a model reason.

choices.text: `h01` is mislabelled
choices.why: Money to the wrong card is the accounts desk's to fix.

prompt: After `h01` fails, a colleague adds a fourteenth rule: *A refund to the wrong card is billing.* What does the lesson suggest instead?

choices.text: Add it, and a fifteenth for the next case
choices.why: That moves the edge to the next case, every time.

choices.text: Describe what billing is for, in the guide
choices.why: Right, and then measure whether the model uses it.

choices.text: Put the new rule in capitals so it outranks line 18
choices.why: Capitals rank rules; they do not settle the conflict.

choices.text: Remove `h01` from the holdout
